title: SiFive
summary: San Francisco company selling RISC-V processor IP as an open alternative to proprietary cores.
bodyHtml:
SiFive develops RISC-V CPU cores and platform IP that chip designers license and integrate. RISC-V is an open instruction set, so customers avoid the licensing constraints of proprietary architectures.

The company's growth tracks the widening use of custom silicon in AI, automotive and embedded systems.

Why it matters

  • RISC-V CPU IP
  • Custom SoC platforms
  • Automotive and AI designs

businessMeaning: RISC-V is becoming the default for custom chips that do not need x86 or Arm compatibility. IP vendors earn before the chip ships, which makes them an early read on design activity.
investmentLens: Private; Arm's listed results are the closest benchmark for the IP-licensing model.
